open_points.subject: M18 FlowActivation / M26 EffectAttempt.authority
open_points.text: "the authority is named by its identity: ... a flow activation by its position in the store's order (M18)"
open_points.question: What exact stable identifier must represent a FlowActivation record when EffectAttempt.authority points to it?
options: Add an explicit flow_activation_id field minted at activation time
Define store-order position as an explicit persisted sequence value and use that
open_points.default_guess: Define a persisted monotonic store sequence for FlowActivation and reference that.

open_points.subject: M09 Activation
open_points.text: "each activation is one issued selection; activating the same implementation again is a new record with its own position in the store's order"
open_points.question: How is one Activation record uniquely addressed in product records/inspection if Activation has no explicit identifier field?
options: Use persisted store-order position as the activation identity
open_points.default_guess: Use persisted store-order position as implicit identity.

open_points.subject: M19 Run lifecycle vs release action
open_points.text: "release a failed run ... already released, is refused" and M19 has "released_by, released_at" but lifecycle lists only running/awaiting_approval/pending/succeeded/failed/refused/cancelled
open_points.question: Is release a formal lifecycle transition of Run (and if so to what status), or only one-time metadata on a failed run?
options: Keep run status as failed and model release only by released_at presence
Introduce a separate released terminal status
Introduce a separate release flag/state machine orthogonal to run status
open_points.default_guess: Keep status failed and treat release as one-time metadata detected by released_at.

open_points.subject: M27 Actor (agent identity over time)
open_points.text: "agent_name ... names are unique in an installation" and "the owner's actions, each agent's and the kernel's own are distinguishable in every record"
open_points.question: Can an agent name be reused after token revocation/replacement, and if yes how are old vs new agents with the same name distinguished in records?
options: Forbid reuse of an agent_name forever within an installation history
Allow reuse and treat same name as same actor identity
Allow reuse but include immutable token fingerprint/version in Actor identity
open_points.default_guess: Forbid reusing an agent_name once it has appeared in records.
